item.title: 5 Near-Perfect City-Builder Games No One Remembers Today
item.description:
While not as mainstream as FPS or RPGs, city-builder games have been around for a long time; seriously, the genre dates back to 1964's The Sumerian Game . Cast as essentially an all-seeing god who takes control of the lives of puny humans, the appeal of city builders is not hard to understand; the games can range from epic sci-fi operas to quirky small-scale fantasy distractions. Most people know SimCity , Anno , Cities: Skylines , and Pharaoh , but a few fantastic city-builders have succumbed to the passage of time, becoming little more than footnotes in history.

The great thing about city builders is that you really don't have to be incredible at them to have a blast. Heck, sometimes doing a terrible job can be more entertaining, and you often feel like you are learning on the job. Personally, I wouldn't consider myself a master of the genre by any means, but I easily lose hours playing any of these upcoming gems.

Emperor: Rise of the Middle Kingdom Is Sierra's Crown Jewel

Perfecting A Stellar City-Building Formula

In the late 90s, Sierra, Impressions Games, and BreakAway Games established the Walker 2D city-builder formula with titles like Caesar 3 , Pharaoh , and Zeus: Master of Olympus , all of which are nowadays readily available on Steam. For one reason or another, the last entry in this run, Emperor: Rise of the Middle Kingdom , never made the jump to Valve's platform and can only be picked up through GOG. Obviously, Good Old Games is fantastic, but if a release isn't on Steam, it might as well not exist for most players.

Emperor: Rise of the Middle Kingdom finally fixed nearly all the issues found in its spiritual predecessors . Unlike in the older games, Emperor gives you way more microscopic control over your citizens and responders, ensuring they don't just wander off onto side roads without reason. It also features a far more expansive agriculture system that goes beyond just dropping a farm and reaping the benefits, as players have to take into account rotations and even weather patterns.

Also, the game is kind of gorgeous! Yes, the graphics are very early-2000s, but the art style and architecture are absolutely timeless and jaw-dropping. Emperor really is the full package, and it might have fared better if it hadn't been released in 2002, just as the genre shifted to 3D graphics.

9 Best Open-World Games That Let You Reshape The World With Creativity, Ranked

From Valheim to Fallout, these open-world games give players the power to reshape terrain, build from scratch, and leave creative marks on worlds.

4
By Mark Sammut

Startopia Lets You Manage A Space Station

And It Is Incredible

Let's shift focus to a forgotten sci-fi game built by a developer with one of the weirdest resumes in video game history. Created by programmers who worked with Bullfrog Productions, the team behind classics like Theme Hospital and Dungeon Keeper , Mucky Foot Productions completed three projects: Urban Chaos , Startopia , and Blade 2 . The two action games were both pretty underwhelming, but they sandwiched one of the more innovative and impressive releases of the early 2000s.

Although not exclusively a city-builder, Startopia blends the genre's tenets with management sim elements , creating a whole that fits both categories and could also qualify as something entirely new. Instead of historical roads or modern grids, your canvas is a metropolis on a space station with finite space. The station has three decks with unique rules, and you need to cater to all three in their own ways. In the meantime, you cannot ignore oxygen, waste management, and recreation.

A big part of what makes Startopia great is its alien species, as the workers aren't just faceless, interchangeable units. The game has 9 core playable species, along with a few other visitors, each with their own strengths, preferences, and baggage.

Immortal Cities: Children of the Nile Flows Like A River

A Great City-Builder Game Created By Genre Veterans

Born from the ashes of Impressions Games, Tilted Mill Entertainment decided to return to Ancient Egypt, as that setting worked so well in Pharaoh . However, Immortal Cities: Children of the Nile isn't just a rethread with 3D graphics, but rather a complete revamp of the city-building formula that discards the ways of old to embrace something new and exciting.

You take charge of a civilization that lives at the mercy of the Nile's annual flooding , along with its other seasonal changes. Rather than presenting city-building as a static grid puzzle, civilization adapts to the current situation, with every season naturally flowing into the next. As money doesn't really have much value in an agrarian society, currency takes the form of grain and food rations.

Immortal Cities: Children of the Nile has an enhanced edition on Steam that is only $7.99. Give it a go if you are looking for an old-school but forward-thinking city builder.

CivCity: Rome Combines Civilization With Stronghold & Caesar

A Fusion Of Greatness

Developed by the strategy super team of Firefly Studios ( Stronghold and Caesar ) and Firaxis Games ( Civilization ), CivCity: Rome sought to bring together two very different types of games. The result was an experimental city builder that struggled to market itself, with the "Civ" branding simultaneously setting the wrong expectations and putting off folks who didn't want a Civilization game.

CivCity essentially tried to fuse Civilization 's tech trees with Firefly's street-level simulation , crafting a game that would cover both the macro and micro. Not everything about the marriage works, but Rome provides one of the more intimate looks into the Roman Empire, letting you see into buildings in impressive detail for the time. The tech tree element arrived in the form of the Academy and Library, where you can research technologies that will help your civilization and reshape the city's layout.

Best City Builders For Android Mobile Devices, Ranked

Fans of city builders who also own an Android device can enjoy the following games.

By John Cunningham

​​​​​​​Tropico 2: Pirate Cove Lets You Be The Pirate King

And The Crown Is Heavy

Tropico doesn't need any introduction, but most people are familiar with Haemimont's later entries, starting with the third game. Tropico 2 sits as the franchise's odd duck, not really fitting its predecessor or successors, as Frog City decided to tear up the first game's foundation in search of something fresh. This shift has helped Tropico 2 age more gracefully than its sequels, simply because it doesn't feel like a worse version of Tropico 5 and 6 .

Tropico 2 completely rejects democracy, instead putting you in charge of governing two populations that are actively against each other: Pirates and Captives. As the Pirate King, players need to balance fear and order. On the one hand, you need to scare the Captives enough to keep them in line; conversely, pirates don't respond well to state control, and you could end up with anarchy if you go too far. Even the economy is unique, as it is built on ship raids.

item.title: Super Expensive, Time-Limited World of Warcraft 12.1.5 Release Officially Revealed
item.description:
World of Warcraft 's 12.1.5 patch is going to feature an extraordinarily expensive, customizable mount that players can only get for a short time. Patch 12.1.5 will introduce new story quests and content to World of Warcraft , such as the new The Promise of Tomorrow story campaign, the Unbinding of Kith'ix raid with just one boss, Labyrinths, and more. Midnight wasn't a universal success, and some players didn't like the many class changes and the new focus on housing elements, so patch 12.1.5 has a lot to prove.

World of Warcraft nerfed its best specs in Curse of Ula'tek, which was the recent 12.1 update, so it's unclear what the meta will be in the next release. Still, Curse of Ula'tek provided fans with a lot of new content, including a whole new zone to explore, and the next update doesn't seem light on features and additions either. Blizzard released an article about WoW's 12.1.5 patch to showcase what's coming, but one of its most exciting additions has been datamined by fans, and it's a brand-new mount with player-selected vendors.

World of Warcraft Officially Brings Back Must-Have Item, and It's Completely Free

World of Warcraft just brough back one of the rarest and most popular rewards in the game completely for free.

By Andrea Trama

World of Warcraft 12.1.5 Update Officially Adds 5-Million Customizable Mount

World of Warcraft players have datamined the new Sporebearer Fungal Strider mount coming with patch 12.1.5, which features two vendors from a selection of four, and costs a whopping 5 million gold plus 500,000 gold for a Transmogrifier and 1,500,000 gold for an Auction House NPC. The mount comes with the Repair vendor and Mail Courier when purchased for 5 million gold, but it can be customized with a Transmogrifier and/or Auction House NPC in place of the existing ones. This can be done at any time through Hoshena, an NPC located near the original mount vendor, Showena, in the Den in World of Warcraft 's Harandar. Any combination of these four vendors can be chosen, but if players want to purchase both the Transmogrifier and Auction House NPCs alongside the mount itself, they will need to fork out a total of 7 million gold. On top of that, the mount will only be available during the Midnight expansion.

From a conceptual standpoint, this mount is similar to the infamous $90 Trader's Gilded Brutosaur in World of Warcraft , but it's arguably even more expensive. While it can be obtained completely free of charge, the 5-million price point is inherently prohibitive for most players. At that point, the only way to get the mount is to purchase multiple WoW Game Time Tokens, which award players with 30 days of game time if they use them, but can also be sold to other players at a variable rate. Currently, players can purchase WoW Tokens for $20 in the US, but they have a rate of 1:238,909 gold at the time of writing. If one wanted to get 7 million through Tokens, they would need to buy between 29 and 30 Tokens, for a total of around $600. Even if one only wanted the base mount without the customizable vendors, the cost would be equivalent to around 21 Tokens in the US, which is still $420.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Fans Should Mark September 8 on their Calendars
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering fans officially have a reason to be excited for September 8, with Wizards of the Coast preparing to pull back the curtain on its newest set, Reality Fracture. The debut stream is expected to be packed with reveals for Magic: The Gathering 's next expansion.

2026 has been a huge year for Magic: The Gathering , releasing a number of highly-anticipated sets. Wizards of the Coast has already returned the game to two fan-favorite planes from Magic 's past, welcoming the launch of Lorwyn Eclipsed in January and Secrets of Strixhaven in April. Crossovers have also been a central focus for the TCG in 2026, launching collaborations with Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles , Marvel Super Heroes , and The Hobbit throughout the year. Now, Magic: The Gathering is putting the spotlight on its final in-universe set of the year.

Magic: The Gathering Officially Bans Multiple Cards, Including a $60 Mythic

Magic: The Gathering just banned several cards across two formats and made restrictions on another, making a rare Mythic unusable.

By Andrea Trama

Magic: The Gathering Teases Reality Fracture Debut Stream

  • September 8, 10 a.m. PT

Wizards of the Coast has officially revealed the date and time for Magic: The Gathering 's Debut Stream for the upcoming Reality Fracture set. The livestream presentation is expected to provide fans with plenty of details about both new cards and the different types of sealed Magic: The Gathering products releasing as part of the expansion, diving into popular planeswalker Jace's alternate "Echoverse." The trailer showcases an eerie depiction of Jace amidst the fracturing images of some of Magic 's most iconic characters, including Ajani, Chandra, and Liliana. Magic: The Gathering 's Reality Fracture Debut Stream will air on September 8 at 10:00 a.m. PT on the game's official Twitch and YouTube channels.

Reality Fracture is set to be a particularly unique expansion for Magic: The Gathering following its release in early October. The set centers around the previously mentioned Echoverse, an alternate universe created by Jace where the Phyrexians and Eldrazi never existed. The expansion will feature matching alternate versions of multiple popular characters in different colors from their usual identities, including a blue variant of Chandra and a white variant of Liliana. The set will even introduce an entire alternate version of Magic: The Gathering 's school of Strixhaven, with Hexhaven having a more militaristic approach than Strixhaven's focus on magic and the arts.

While fan excitement grows for Magic 's next set, Wizards of the Coast has shared some disappointing news about the expansion. The company confirmed in late August that it is facing early supply issues with Reality Fracture's North American release, announcing that Play Booster boxes of the set may only be available in limited quantities at launch. The shortage is not expected to affect any products other than Play Boosters, with ancillary products such as Collector Boosters, Commander Decks, and Pre-release Packs planned to ship as normal.

Brand-New $850 Magic: The Gathering Release Officially Available Now
Magic: The Gathering Officially Bans Multiple Cards, Including a $60 Mythic

Magic: The Gathering has already given fans plenty of reason to be excited about the future of the game. Wizards of the Coast confirmed during MagicCon Amsterdam that three in-universe Magic sets will release in 2027, showing off a brand-new plane and new takes on classic locations. Nauctis: The Sunken Realm will kick off the year, introducing a new plane centered on the titular sub-aquatic kingdom. Kamigawa: Titanbreach will see the mechs of Kamigawa clashing with the monsters of Ikoria, while Zhalfir will put the focus on Afro-fantasy for the plane's first starring role. With new planes and returning classic settings, 2027 looks set to be another big year for Magic: The Gathering .

Kamigawa: Titanbreach will see the mechs of Kamigawa clashing with the monsters of Ikoria, while Zhalfir will put the focus on Afro-fantasy for the plane's first starring role. With new planes and returning classic settings, 2027 looks set to be another big year for Magic: The Gathering .

item.title: Alien: Isolation 2 Is Walking Right Into One of the Biggest Challenges in Survival Horror Games
item.description:
Survival horror fans have been eating insanely good for the better part of the last decade, with every franchise, IP, and setting imaginable receiving a terrifying experience for all to enjoy. In the midst of all the Resident Evil and Silent Hill games, it felt like there was one horror sequel missing in the sci-fi department, but now, the wait for Alien: Isolation 2 is almost over, to the relief of fans who have been waiting since 2014. However, the industry has changed a lot in that time, and if this new game is to succeed, then it has to learn from the biggest mistakes of the original and those of the wider genre—that being pacing and length.

In order to keep your players invested and scared for the entire runtime of a game, you need to carefully plan out the narrative arcs and twists from start to finish. That also means that the story has to begin and conclude in a timely manner; if you start crossing over the 20-hour mark without a good reason, the fear factor can dwindle, and the fatigue really sets in. Looking back at the first game, length was often the only major complaint people had about it, and now, with Alien: Isolation 2 on the horizon, I'm concerned that we may end up in a similar situation where the actual gameplay and atmosphere are incredible, but the duration ticks past its expiration date and ends up feeling like a slog rather than a satisfying journey.

Sequels Keep Getting Bigger, But This New Survival Horror Game Got Better by Being Smaller

Sequels often expand the scope of the first game, but this new survival horror title perfectly demonstrates how less can be more.

By LB Beistad

Alien: Isolation 2 Needs to Avoid the Genre's Biggest Issue

Making a good survival horror game is no easy feat, what with all the competition and the high expectations of the fans who have played just about every major release there is to play. You need to have a great hook right from the get-go, interesting enemies and combat, a compelling story, good world-building, and a tidy ending that closes things out before they overstay their welcome. If you manage to nail all of those components, then you end up with a virtually perfect horror game, but if you fail in even one regard, then the whole experience can be soured.

That's exactly how I felt about Alien: Isolation when I first played it. I was immediately captivated by the thought of being hunted by a terrifying and intelligent Xenomorph, and while I was a little late to the party, judging by the reviews and the sales numbers, I was hoping for a real home-run finish. Yet, when I got to the middle of the game, having already spent a dozen or so hours exploring and progressing through the station, I started thinking that things were getting a bit repetitive, and when I looked at how much more game I had to conquer, my excitement became nonexistent when I saw I had about the same amount of time to go.

If you start crossing over the 20-hour mark, the fear factor can dwindle, and the fatigue really sets in.

This is the core issue that a lot of otherwise great horror games run into that is only really an issue within this specific genre. The whole point is to keep the stress level high and to subvert the player's expectations, but if you have absorbed the atmosphere and gotten comfortable with the feel of the game over a longer period of time, then it can be a lot harder to feel afraid. And, if the story doesn't have a reason to go on and the runtime is being padded by additional exploration and unnecessary backtracking, then the overall quality of the game becomes a lot lower when you compare how things started versus how they ended.

Also, survival horror specifically focuses some of its attention on weaponry, where in the early sections, you might have a weak pistol with a limited ammo supply, but as the game opens up and you start to progress to the later sections, suddenly that shoddy arsenal looks more like a military-grade cabinet capable of taking down anything that moves. What that means for longer games is that you either have to level up the action and give players more engaging segments, like in Resident Evil 4 , or wind things down before that struggling survivor becomes a capable killing machine.

The Best Horror Games Value Quality Over Quantity

If we look at the highest rated games in the survival horror genre, they all have one thing in common: a solid length to quality ratio. The actual problem isn't necessarily games being too long, it is how the developers fill out the playthrough, which means every piece of gameplay from the first few interactions, all the way until the credits roll. Some of the scariest and most stressful games, like Silent Hill 2 and Alan Wake 2, actually push the duration into the 15–20 hour region, and Resident Evil 4 , arguably the greatest survival horror game ever made, is known for being decently long as well. However, in all these cases, the runtime always feels purposeful rather than filler.

You can even go the other way, and turn to much more recent releases such as Resident Evil Requiem or Silent Hill f , both of which can be beaten in under 10 hours without rushing. That may seem short, yet in that time, they deliver some horrifying moments and insane segments of action that just wouldn't hit the same if the games were significantly longer. As nice as it was to revisit Raccoon City and as atmospheric as some of the spiritual dream sequences were, I felt as though the stories had run their course and the fear was nearing its end point, so I was content with the playthroughs being on the midrange section of the spectrum.

At the same time, there is such a thing as too little game. One of my favorite modern survival horror games is Scorn, but as much as I adore the world building and the art direction, beating the game in under three hours felt a little bit underwhelming. The same can be said for Bad Cheese , a Disney-inspired horror game that I was very excited to get my hands on, that also ended in a single session. In these instances, I had a great time with the content given, yet was hoping there would be a lot more, as in that amount of time, you aren't really developing the story too much, and it feels as though you are exiting the world just as quickly as you entered.

New Survival Horror Game on Steam is Division Meets Fallout with a Unique Jurassic Park Twist
Alien: Isolation 2 is Following in the Footsteps of the More Open Outlast Games
Alien Isolation 2: How the Survival Horror Genre Has Evolved in the 12 Years Since the First One

The line of time is fine and hard to pin down. There is no one formula that will work for every game, and I do believe that there is a good case for longer and shorter games in different circumstances. It comes down to whether the story and the action within it has a reason to conclude when it does and if it is worth continuing things a bit longer to tie up the final strands of the narrative. For now, we will have to wait and see if Alien: Isolation 2 manages to fix that issue from the original game, but in the meantime, there are plenty of other sci-fi and general survival horror games to dig into that get the pacing right and only leave you wanting more at the end.

item.title: Square Enix Comments on Final Fantasy 7 Remake's Future
item.description:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation game director Naoki Hamaguchi stated during a recent panel that he wanted the Final Fantasy 7 Remake saga to continue beyond the current game trilogy as a way to pass it along to future generations. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is arguably one of the most anticipated games releasing in 2027.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation was first unveiled during Summer Game Fest 2026, as Hamaguchi shared a glimpse of what fans can expect in the climactic finale of the FF7 Remake saga. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation 's combat system will include new FITS based on some iconic Jobs from the Final Fantasy series to offer new ways that players can customize their favorite characters. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will launch on April 8 on all current-gen platforms simultaneously. Pre-orders for FF7 Revelation are now available on the Square Enix Store and other storefronts.

Final Fantasy 14 Fans May Have Figured Out Evercold's Second New Job

Final Fantasy 14 players point out a string of clues that could possibly identify what Evercold's new ranged physical DPS job will be.

By James Ratcliff

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Director Wants to Continue FF7 Saga

Although the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series has seen some spin-off characters return to the story, Square Enix stated it may not be done with the saga yet. At PAX West 2026 in Seattle, Hamaguchi and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation battle director Teruki Endo hosted an hour-long panel called "From Reunion to Resolve: Designing the FF7 Remake Trilogy." Hamaguchi said that Square Enix wanted to expand the future of Final Fantasy 7 and move it to becoming an IP that will continue to evolve over time. Hamaguchi also added that the Final Fantasy 7 Remake was made with the intention of re-telling the story and themes of Final Fantasy 7 for new generations to discover and to tailor these experiences to modern times.

However, Hamaguchi did not state what the evolution of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake series would precisely entail. As part of the ongoing story of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake game trilogy, Square Enix has also used spin-off titles like Crisis Core Reunion and Ever Crisis as ways to tell the backstories of popular characters, such as Sephiroth and Zack Fair. Though Crisis Core Reunion was released in late 2022, other games in the Final Fantasy 7 compilation have not been ported to modern platforms as of this writing.

During the panel, Hamaguchi and Endo also shared more details about Final Fantasy 7 Revelation 's battle system, including how some FITS tie into each character's established skill sets. Using Vincent Valentine as one example, Hamaguchi and Endo stated that equipping him with a Summoner outfit would allow him to use his Galian Beast form to create coordinated attacks with the Ifrit summon. Given that Vincent and Cid will finally be playable in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation , time will tell how players utilize them in battle.

It remains to be seen if other Final Fantasy 7 spin-offs will receive modern ports or if new games altogether will be made following the launch of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation .
